newsitem.title: UK: MFI extends losses on talk of downgrades.
newsitem.headline: MFI extends losses on talk of downgrades.

text.p: Shares in MFI Furniture Group Plc extended their losses on Tuesday amid talk that at least four brokers downgraded the stock after the UK retailer issued a disappointing trading statement.
By 1015 GMT, the shares were down 40-1/2p, or 20 percent, to 156-1/2. They were the fourth most actively traded shares in London, with more than 10.2 million shares changing hands.
The shares were trading at their lowest level in a year.
Talk of downgrades came after the UK retailer warned it had not seen a sustained increase in demand, and said its sales had slowed since the first half.
HSBC James Capel analyst Jenny Nips said she downgraded the stock, but declined to provide details.
Dealers said Credit Lyonnais Laing, NatWest Markets and SBC Warburg also downgraded the stock. Analysts there weren't immediately available to comment.
